messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT • us-west-2 /v1/stream • p99=1.80s (SLO=0.50s) • streaming stalls detected • affected sessions=32 • paging oncall @oncall-anna :rotating_light:

oncall-anna: acked — I'm on the page. linking alerts, starting triage. anyone seeing related deploys?

sre-devon: looking at infra metrics now. GPU host gpu-node-173 in cluster-usw2 shows rising ECC correctables + thermal margin drop. K80/RTX-series? looks like an A100 host, sustained 94-96C for last 8m and firmware thermal throttle events.

eng-ml-raj: we see KV cache miss spike and retry backpressure in streaming workers. requests piling up on long tail (we're seeing stalled chunk flushes). likely due to degraded accelerator throughput.

infra-ashley: if GPU is thermal-throttling that's going to blow up throughput for streaming. recommend immediate evacuation: cordon + drain node gpu-node-173 and move pods to warm pool. I'll prep the replacement host.

oncall-anna: actioning evacuation now. commands I'm running: ```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-node-173
kubectl drain gpu-node-173 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30 --timeout=5m
```

prod-support-jules: tagging affected customers: acct-omega, acct-orion, acct-skb. Replied to acct-omega saying we're investigating and we may route them to backup capacity — will update support thread.

sre-devon: posting quick telemetry snapshot: p95 rose from 120ms->420ms, p99 from 480ms->1.80s across /v1/stream. Streaming stall alerts correlate with ECC correctable spikes: ```
[2026-03-15T12:04:21Z] gpu-node-173 ECC_CORRECTABLE: +17
[2026-03-15T12:05:07Z] gpu-node-173 ECC_CORRECTABLE: +23
[2026-03-15T12:07:12Z] thermal_throttle event count: 4
```

deploy-bot: Canary fallback model variant enabled for route /v1/stream: redwood/llm-small-quantized:v2 (auto-fallback triggered).

eng-ml-raj: quick mitigation suggestion — reduce batching and force synchronous kv-cache checks on workers shard to avoid long tail. Proposed config change: ```yaml
workload: stream
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 256
  max_wait_ms: 15
```
I'll push this to runtime in 60s if no objections.

infra-ashley: agreed. also setting node label gpu.flaky=true so autoscaler avoids it and scheduling won't put pods back. after drain I'll quarantine the node in inventory.

oncall-anna: running live tests — replays to /v1/stream against warm pool NOW. monitoring latency.

sre-devon: after evacuation + fallback + batching tweak: p95=130ms, p99=0.42s, streaming stall count dropped to 2 in last 10m. Looks like routing + fallback helped. :white_check_mark:

prod-support-jules: Updated customers: acct-omega confirmed degraded experience resolved; acct-orion on standby for postmortem. Escalated to account execs per SLA.

eng-ml-raj: note for follow-up: KV cache churn may have amplified impact with one degraded accelerator — we should run a synthetic workload to validate cache warming effects once node is quarantined.

infra-ashley: hardware team paged to inspect gpu-node-173. preliminary suggestion: possible intermittent ECC flake combined with poor airflow on that rack. Plan: quarantine + replace GPU or swap host, run burn-in.

oncall-anna: marking incident as mitigated for now — continuing to monitor for 30m. will transition to post-incident RCA if node confirmed flaky. Thanks all for quick ops. :pray:

sre-devon: logging timeline + artifacts to incidents/5333333333/ for RCA. key next steps: hardware diag, firmware check, heatmap of rack cooling, and revisit batching defaults for streaming.

infra-ashley: I'll coordinate hardware replace and update this thread when the node is physically out of rotation.

prod-support-jules: closing customer-facing advisory stating we routed traffic to fallback and are replacing the host; no data loss; ETA for hardware follow-up 24-48h.

oncall-anna: final note — if we see any reappearance of p99>0.6s in next 30m I'll reopen page. good job team. :tada:
